about: Every decision Bootstrap settles before it writes the answers file. `ask` says when the target user is asked: always, per-environment, on-evidence (only when discovery finds the thing), or derived (filled from discovery and approved in the grouped defaults). `recommend` is a proposal to state with the evidence found, never an answer. `answers` is where the result goes in the answers file; `slots` and `tokens` are the payload slots and host capability tokens the decision fills.

questions.question: Which clients will the team use in this repository, and on which surfaces (terminal, IDE extension, desktop or web app)?
questions.recommend: Only the clients the team actually uses. Multi-select from the client profiles (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, OpenCode, Cursor) or Other with a name. Never select a client because Bootstrap runs in it or because its folder exists.

questions.question: Which client runs this Bootstrap session?
questions.recommend: Record it separately from the selected clients; it selects nothing.

questions.question: Is Node.js available to every client that will run the roles?
questions.recommend: Required. Without it, the gates run by hand from the contracts and are recorded as instruction-only, and only with the user's explicit approval.

questions.question: Should Bootstrap stop at the file plan, or install after approval?
questions.recommend: Install after approval of the file plan.

questions.question: Which repository name do the root instructions announce?
questions.recommend: The package manifest name; otherwise the git remote name; otherwise the folder name.

questions.question: Which prefix should the generated role agents and role skills carry?
questions.recommend: A short slug of the repository name with a trailing hyphen, for example `shop-` for `shop-web`, because names like `ask` or `orchestrator` collide easily with other agent sets. An empty prefix keeps the canonical names.
infer_from: existing agent and skill names in the selected clients' folders

questions.question: How do users start the user roles (orchestrator, ask, knowledge-builder) in this client?
questions.recommend: The profile's default route, confirmed on every surface the team uses: native agents only when the client's agent picker works on all of them; otherwise role skills invoked by name. One route per client, never both.
infer_from: the surfaces named in the environments answer

questions.question: How does the orchestrator start its delegates in this client?
questions.recommend: Native subagents, each with its own context. Only a client without subagents uses a separate CLI process (the profile's `subprocess` command); if it has neither, the workflows are blocked in that client. Never inline.

questions.question: Does the current documentation of each selected client still match its profile?
questions.recommend: Re-read the profile's `docs`. Record every difference (a folder, a tool name, a field) as an override and say why; the installer applies overrides on top of the profile.
infer_from: the profile's `docs` at their current version

questions.question: Which work-item tracker does this repository use?
questions.recommend: The tracker the team already uses, reached through an MCP server or integration already configured for the selected clients; the local Markdown tracker when there is none.
infer_from: tracker references in CONTRIBUTING.md and PR templates

questions.question: Which exact tools read work items (item, type, linked titles, comments) and, when manage-work-item is generated, create and update them?
questions.recommend: Only the tracker integration's single-item, type, batch, comment, create and update operations, returning Markdown. No search, delete or administrative tools. The local Markdown tracker binds them to its contract and the file tools. Register and authenticate the integration per client (contracts/integrations.md).
infer_from: configured MCP servers and their tool lists per client

questions.question: Generate the manage-work-item skill (create bugs and user stories, update existing items)?
questions.recommend: Generate it when a write binding works; skip or defer it otherwise, rather than installing a skill that cannot write.

questions.question: Which wiki does the orchestrator read, and with which tools?
questions.recommend: Ask only when discovery finds a wiki (GitHub wiki, Confluence, a Notion space…). Otherwise record `{ "none": "no wiki" }` and the orchestrator skips those calls.
infer_from: wiki links in README and docs

questions.question: How do the orchestrator, ask and knowledge-builder look at an image in this client, including an image attached to a work item?
questions.recommend: The role's own image-capable read tool, with the bytes fetched through an authorized integration for issue attachments; a cheaper vision-capable delegate only when the user approves the model. When an image cannot be read, the role asks the user for it.

questions.question: Which other MCP or client tools should a role have (documentation, cloud, design tools…)?
questions.recommend: Only exact, least-privilege tools that a role needs and the repository already uses. On the skill route they are made available at client level.
infer_from: package manifests that name external APIs or frameworks

questions.question: Which repository folder holds the runtime, its config, the workflows and the contracts?
questions.recommend: `.agentic-system/`, tracked in git so a clone works. Use the visible `agentic-system/` when a selected client cannot read hidden folders.

questions.question: Where should the session folders (memory, log, artifacts, designs) live?
questions.recommend: Outside the repository, `~/.agentic-system/sessions/<repo-name>`: sessions are per developer and never pollute the repository. Alternative: a repository folder such as `.agentic-system-sessions/`, ignored by git. Outside paths are written with `~` and every client gets permission to reach them.

questions.question: Which per-user folder holds personal documentation templates?
questions.recommend: `~/.agentic-system`.

questions.question: Where should the example documentation templates go: the user folder (personal) or the workspace folder (shared through git)?
questions.recommend: The user folder; team templates the repository shares go in the workspace folder `<runtime root>/documentation/templates/`.

questions.question: Which repository folder holds the project knowledge?
questions.recommend: `knowledge/`, tracked. Existing docs stay where they are; knowledge-builder writes tiered documents here that reference them.

questions.question: Where is the repository vocabulary glossary?
questions.recommend: The existing `CONTEXT.md` or `GLOSSARY.md`; otherwise `CONTEXT.md` at the root, created by knowledge-builder when there are terms to record, never just because it is missing.

questions.question: Which commands validate a change?
questions.recommend: The lint, typecheck, test and build commands CI runs, in CI's order.
infer_from: package.json scripts, Makefile, pyproject.toml, build files

questions.question: Which repository folder holds the installation records (answers, manifest, baselines)?
questions.recommend: `.agentic-system-maintenance/`, tracked so anyone on the team can run maintenance, and never read by the roles.

questions.question: Where do the human guides for each client go?
questions.recommend: `docs/agentic-system/`, tracked; or the repository's existing documentation folder convention.
